## Summary

- Adds daily paper summary for 2026-05-19
- Paper: **Practical Scaling Laws: Converting Compute into Performance in a Data-Constrained World** (arXiv:2605.09189)
- Authors: Christopher M. Bryant and Hao Liu (Arena Physica), submitted May 9, 2026
- Updates README.md with new entry at the top

## Paper highlights

Chinchilla's scaling law — the dominant guide for allocating compute between model size and training data — was calibrated for data-rich, single-epoch pretraining and has three structural failures outside that regime: it diverges as data shrinks, cannot express overfitting, and conflates unique data count D with total training steps T.

This paper proposes a corrected closed-form formula L(N, D, T) = E + (L₀ − E)·h/(1+h) that decomposes loss into undercapacity, undertraining, and overfitting terms, reduces to Chinchilla in the original regime, and is validated across four architecture families (MLPs, ResNets, Fourier Neural Operators, Transformers) covering vision, scientific ML, and language domains.

author: ianblenke
body:
## Summary

Builds on PR #195's Q4_K → Q4_K passthrough by adding **Q8_0 source preservation** for the 251 attn / deltanet / shared-expert weights in Unsloth's \`Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_M.gguf\` that ship as Q8_0 for higher precision than Q4_K.

Before: \`GGUF Q8_0 → dequant to f32 → quantize to Q4_K (lossy downquantization)\`.
After: round-trips as Q8_0 byte-for-byte.

## Verification

Tested on Qwen 3.6 35B-A3B greedy chat completion (\"Hi\" prompt):

| | v5 (no Q8_0 passthrough) | v9 (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| First decoded token | \"1\" (garbage) | **\"Hello\"** (coherent) |
| Output | \"1 1 1 1...\" | \"Hello!     1 1 1...\" |

Residual-stream pearson vs llama.cpp's \`l_out-N.bin\` improves at every layer:

| Layer | v5 pearson | v9 pearson | Δ |
|------:|-----------:|-----------:|--:|
|   0   | 0.9937 | 0.9967 | +0.003 |
|   4   | 0.9831 | 0.9849 | +0.002 |
|  22   | 0.9918 | 0.9929 | +0.001 |
|  30   | 0.9160 | 0.9262 | +0.010 |
|  31   | 0.6235 | 0.6504 | +0.027 |
|  35   | 0.1497 | 0.1715 | +0.022 |
|  38   | -0.5361 | -0.5051 | +0.031 |

L0 attn_qkv manifest shows \`format: \"Q8_0\"\` with length 17,825,792 B (= 8192 rows × 64 super-blocks × 34 bytes ✓ for Q8_0). Deltanet bin grew 1.89× (Q8_0 is 2.13 bpw vs Q4_K's 1.12 bpw — exact ratio match).

## Changes

- \`QuantBlockFormat::Q8_0\` enum variant (serde \`\"Q8_0\"\`)
- \`quant::registry\` Q8_0 entry: \`block_elements=32\`, \`bytes_per_block=34\`, \`row_dot=q8_0_row_dot\`
- \`try_q4k_passthrough\` widened to accept Q8_0 target
- New \`try_preserve_quant_passthrough(source, key)\`: picks the source's native format, validates, returns \`(bytes, format, rows, cols)\`
- \`attn.rs\` / \`deltanet.rs\` writers gain a Tier-2 passthrough arm: preserve source format when higher-precision than target
- \`convert_cmd.rs\` lazy-loader scan widened to Q4_K / Q5_K / Q6_K / Q8_0, but **excludes** \`token_embd.weight\` / \`output.weight\` / \`lm_head.weight\` (which have special extract paths that assume dense f32 storage)
- \`qwen35_load_vindex.rs\` populator: \`\"Q8_0\" => TYPE_Q8_0\` in format-string match arms (no longer falls through to silent \`continue\`)
- \`feature_major_down\` returns explicit error for Q8_0 (it's an FFN-only writer that shouldn't reach Q8_0 storage)

## Still to do (not in this PR)

1. **MoE expert path** (\`moe_layers.rs\`'s \`quantize_dense_entry\`) re-quantizes through f32 even when source is Q4_K. The interleaved gate+up packing in the writer is not a simple byte passthrough; needs a layout-preserving fast path.
2. **lm_head Q6_K passthrough** — currently goes through \`write_lm_head_q4k\` which always emits \`TENSOR_Q4K\` kind. Q6_K storage needs a separate kind in the lm_head manifest path.
3. The model **still degenerates after a few coherent tokens**, so Q8_0 was a necessary but not sufficient fix. The MoE FFN re-quantization (item 1) is the most likely next contributor.

author: whitekid
body:
## Summary

Phase 1 of the large-object chunking redesign: every object now persists as a sequence of one or more `SegmentRef` instead of a single flat file. PUT/GET stream through 8-worker chunker/fetcher pipelines producing 16 MiB chunks. Internal segment integrity moves from MD5 to xxhash3-128 (10-20 GiB/s vs ~500 MiB/s), eliminating dual hashing on the hot path. Range GET, sendfile zero-copy, multipart, AppendObject, packblob, and PITR snapshot/restore stay correct under the new layout.

**Architectural changes**

- New segment-based storage model — `Object.segments:[SegmentRef]` always populated
- Streaming PUT pipeline (`SegmentWriter`) + parallel GET pipeline (`SegmentReader`) bounded to ~144 MiB / ~128 MiB per request regardless of object size
- xxhash3-128 segment integrity, MD5 only at S3 protocol boundary
- Per-segment AAD encryption isolation verified
- `PackedBackend` implements `PartialIO` — Range GET works across pack threshold
- PITR snapshot/restore propagates segments + checks segment paths

body:
## Summary

Implements the OpenSpec change `add-scenario-objective-engine` end-to-end. Generated combat scenarios could previously only be won by total destruction; this builds the objective-hex spatial system so a procedurally generated scenario can be played to a non-destruction outcome (Capture / Defend / Breakthrough).

## What was implemented

- **Objective data model** — `IObjectiveMarker`, `HexKey`, `ObjectiveControlRule`, `IObjectiveOutcome` in `ScenarioInterfaces.ts`; `objectives: Record<HexKey, IObjectiveMarker>` carried on `IGameState` (design D1 — `IHex` unchanged). A markerless map behaves identically to today.
- **Placement** — `ScenarioGenerator` (and the `SimulationRunner` path) place objective hexes per type, seeded deterministically from the scenario seed. Capture → 1–3 interior hexes; Defend → defender deployment zone; Breakthrough → exit edge opposite the attacker.
- **Control detection** — `detectObjectiveControl` / `advanceObjectiveControl` implement the sole-occupancy rule with sticky-on-contest control (design D3) and per-turn `holdProgress` advancement.
- **Victory evaluation** — `evaluateObjectiveOutcome` covers Destroy / Capture / Defend / Breakthrough (design D5), consulted before the destruction fallback in `checkVictoryConditions`, `GameOutcomeCalculator`, and `SimulationRunner` (design D4). An objective win overrides a turn-limit draw and surviving units.
- **Rendering** — read-only `ObjectiveMarkersLayer` in `HexMapDisplay`, above terrain and below tokens (design D6), styled by control state (neutral / friendly / enemy / contested) with Capture hold-progress display.
- **Lifecycle events** — `ObjectiveCaptured` / `ObjectiveLost` / `ObjectiveProgress` event types + payloads; emitted by the per-turn control pass and applied by a reducer so the event log fully replays objective state (design D7).

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — zero errors
- `npx oxlint src/` — 0 warnings, 0 errors
- `npx oxfmt --check` — all new/changed files clean
- `npx openspec validate add-scenario-objective-engine --strict` — valid
- Tests — 51 new objective tests (unit + integration + render); full gameplay/simulation/component/service suites green (8900+ tests, 0 failures)

## Notes / deviations

- `GameOutcomeCalculator` keeps its richer `elimination` / `mutual_destruction` reason labels for markerless scenarios — only a true objective-marker win (Capture / Defend / Breakthrough) short-circuits with reason `objective`. Routing markerless `destroy` straight through `reason: 'objective'` would have regressed existing post-battle summary semantics; design D5 ("express Destroy through the same engine for uniformity") is honored at the evaluation layer while preserving the calculator's label contract.
- Task 5.1 names `gameSessionCore` — its game-over logic is `checkVictoryConditions` in `gameStateReducer`, which is the surface that was wired.
- BV parity and determinism untouched: no construction-layer changes; placement uses `SeededRandom` and control detection is a pure function of unit positions.

body:
## Summary

Split a dedicated `HomeComposerRegion` off from `SessionComposerRegion` so the home route can no longer mount session-only docks with stale composer state. Removes the visible 1-frame full-height todo-dock flash that appeared when navigating session → home.

## Why

`session.tsx` is a single route component serving both `/:dir/session` and `/:dir/session/:id`. It constructed one `composer = createSessionComposerState({...})` and passed it into the same `SessionComposerRegion` for both variants. On a session→home transition, the home variant re-mounted while `composer.dock()` was still stale-true from the session view; `useSpring` initialises from the current target on mount (no animate-from-0), so `SessionTodoDock` rendered immediately at full height before the todos effect re-ran and animated it out — a phantom dock collapse on a page that should never show the dock.

The fix moves Home onto a region that never receives `SessionComposerState` and never imports `SessionTodoDock` / `SessionQuestionDock` / `SessionPermissionContent` / `SessionRevertDock` / `SessionFollowupDock`. The boundary is structural, so the next field added to `SessionComposerState` cannot leak the same way.

Plan iteration: 10 review rounds (3× Claude+Codex crosscheck + 5× GPT Pro external) before code was written; final plan at https://github.com/Astro-Han/pawwork/issues/753#issuecomment-4484743928. Post-implementation crosscheck (Claude+Codex) returned 0 P0/P1; P2 findings folded into the cleanup commit.

## Related Issue

Fixes #753

## Human Review Status

Pending

## Review Focus

- The boundary itself: `home-composer-region.tsx` has zero imports from session-only docks and no `SessionComposerState` prop (locked by an import-grep contract test).
- `composerHome` rewire in `session.tsx`: now points at `renderHomeComposerRegion` instead of branching `renderComposerRegion("home", ...)`.
- The narrowed session-only `SessionComposerRegion` still serves child-session "back to parent" + disabled-prompt path (uses `useNavigate`, `useSync`, `useSessionRouteKey` for `route.params.dir` — preserved intentionally; only the `home()` memo and home-only classList branches are removed).
- E2E shape: `packages/app/e2e/session/session-composer-dock.spec.ts:1691` installs a `MutationObserver` on `document.body` BEFORE clicking the sidebar new-session button and asserts zero transient `[data-component="session-todo-dock"]` additions until `[data-component="session-new-home"]` is visible. This catches the one-frame flash that a steady-state `toHaveCount(0)` assertion would miss.

## Risk Notes

- **Known residual, out of scope for this PR**: a fast `session_A → home → session_B` sequence may still mount session_B's region while `composer.dock()` is stale-true from session_A's snapshot. Different navigation pattern, separate flash surface. Will be tracked as a follow-up issue post-merge. The cheapest remedy when it surfaces is a per-call `{ from: 0 }` option on `useSpring` applied at `session-composer-region.tsx`.
- **Skipped conditional — visible UI manual check with screenshots/recordings**: the bug is a 1-frame DOM mutation during a route transition; a static screenshot cannot capture it, and a 25fps video (40ms per frame) would straddle the ~30ms flash window unreliably (a missing capture would not prove the fix; a captured frame would not prove regression). The MutationObserver assertion at `session-composer-dock.spec.ts:1691` is the precise dynamic contract — TDD-verified red against pre-fix code (the dock element was recorded in `addedNodes` during the transition) and green after the split.
- **Skipped conditional — macOS/Windows platform impact**: no platform/packaging/updater/signing/paths/shell/permissions surface was touched. Pure SolidJS route component split.
- **Skipped conditional — docs/release notes/dependencies/permissions/credentials/deletion/generated/local files**: none of those surfaces were touched.

## How To Verify

```text
app typecheck (tsgo -b):           passed
eslint (root lint):                passed
shell-frame-contract test:         9/9 passed (covers the new boundary)
session-composer-dock e2e:         41/41 passed incl. new "todo dock does not flash on home" case
home.spec.ts / theme-helper / a11y-chip e2e: clean (1 pre-existing failure on `active workspace has a check icon` exists on origin/dev too, unrelated)
TDD verification:                  new e2e runs RED on pre-fix code, GREEN after the split (manually stashed impl to confirm)
```

## Screenshots or Recordings

Not applicable — the bug is a single-frame DOM mutation during route transition; static screenshots cannot capture it. The new MutationObserver-based e2e at `packages/app/e2e/session/session-composer-dock.spec.ts:1691` records the dock element being added to the DOM during the transition and asserts it is empty post-fix. Verified red→green.

body:
Follow-up to #4. The new `fetch_flake_source` helper invokes:

\`\`\`
nix flake metadata --json git+ssh://...?rev=<recorded-rev>
\`\`\`

and reads `.path` from the JSON to feed `BUILDER_FLAKE` / `ENCLAVIA_FLAKE`. That call fails on a fresh shell with:

\`\`\`
error: cannot write modified lock file of flake
'git+ssh://...?rev=...' (use '--no-write-lock-file' to ignore)
\`\`\`

…because the fetched flake's transitive inputs aren't all locked at the rev we ask for, and nix's default behaviour is to rewrite the fetched flake's lock to bring them current. The remote URL is read-only, so the write fails and the whole fetch aborts.

We only want the source store path; nothing else here cares about the freshness of the fetched flake's transitive inputs. Pass `--no-write-lock-file` so nix skips the rewrite.

## Test plan

Verified end-to-end against beta: after merging #4, applying the deployment with `FLAKE_LOCK_PATH` set (EnclaviaIO/deployment#15), and building the wrapped builder from EnclaviaIO/builder#22, `enclavia reproduce <new-enclave>` now prints:

\`\`\`
✓ Reproducible — local PCRs match the recorded build.

  PCR0: ff9f2ef6...
  PCR1: df41caf1...
  PCR2: 324bf85d...
\`\`\`

The setfiles -F flag is documented rather confusingly as:
```
  -F  Force reset of context to  match  file_context  for  customizable
      files,  and  the  default  file context, changing the user, role,
      range portion as well as the type.
```
"Customizable types" are an SELinux concept that I'm not very clear about it appears we expect local changes to be made, and for setfiles/fixfiles/restorecon not to reset the label back to default. Gentoo has this page about them:

  https://wiki.gentoo.org/wiki/SELinux/Tutorials/Working_with_customizable_types

It seems that we shouldn't try to modify these labels, and in particular it breaks podman rootless containers.  So drop the -F flag (confusingly called "~force:true").

More precisely, this will make flags->set_specctx be false in the following libselinux code:

  https://github.com/SELinuxProject/selinux/blob/3aac92b7250ed57fd4ab674ffcf03d9c499b3188/libselinux/src/selinux_restorecon.c#L738-L765

To test this change, I used virt-builder to create the following images:

body:
## Why

This PR comes from a measured pass over the GitHub Actions critical path for regular CI and `release-beta`. The immediate use case was to reduce maintainer feedback latency and beta publication time without weakening stable delivery gates.

The pain was that several jobs had become visibly expensive after earlier release hardening:

- CI was spending most of its wall clock in daemon tests and Playwright critical checks.
- `release-beta` was paying for full beta validation, Windows cache maintenance, and a serial final publish step even though beta is the daily R&D validation channel.
- Runtime summaries were not detailed enough to confidently attribute savings by job and step.

## What users will see

No product UI or app behavior changes.

Maintainers will see faster and more attributable GitHub Actions runs:

- CI summaries now expose job and slow-step runtime data.
- Daemon tests run in two shards.
- Playwright critical checks are split into `core` and `starters` jobs.
- `release-beta` publishes platform assets from the platform builder jobs and leaves the final publish job to aggregate metadata.
- Beta `metadata.json` now includes platform readiness fields: `expectedPlatforms`, `readyPlatforms`, `failedPlatforms`, and `releaseState`.
- Partial or failed beta runs publish versioned metadata only; `beta/latest/metadata.json` remains pinned to the last complete beta.
- Beta platform publishing now fails fast when a report-bearing platform has no smoke report files, and metadata verification checks published report evidence.
- Beta Windows smoke no longer verifies running-app direct reinstall by default; full reinstall verification remains the non-beta default.
- `nix-check` is no longer a default PR gate; it remains available on pushes to `main` and manual dispatch for the community Nix installation surface.

## Surface area

- [ ] **UI** — new page / dialog / panel / menu item / setting / empty state in `apps/web` or `apps/desktop` (including Electron menu bar)
- [ ] **Keyboard shortcut** — new or changed
- [ ] **CLI / env var** — new `od` subcommand or flag, new `tools-dev` / `tools-pack` / `tools-pr` flag, or new `OD_*` env var
- [ ] **API / contract** — new `/api/*` endpoint, new SSE event, or changed shape in `packages/contracts`
- [ ] **Extension point** — new entry under `skills/`, `design-systems`, `design-templates`, or `craft/`, or change to the skills protocol
- [ ] **i18n keys** — added new translation keys (see `TRANSLATIONS.md` for the locale workflow)
- [ ] **New top-level dependency** — adding any new entry to the **root** `package.json` (`dependencies` or `devDependencies`); workspace-package `package.json` files are out of scope. Include a paragraph on what we get vs. what bytes we ship (see `CONTRIBUTING.md` -> Code style)
- [ ] **Default behavior change** — changes what existing users experience without opting in (default model, default setting, file/SQLite schema, auto-network on startup, auto-install)
- [x] **None** — internal refactor, docs, tests, or translation update only

## Screenshots

Not applicable; this is workflow/release infrastructure only.

## Bug fix verification

Not a bug fix.

## Validation

Local validation:

- `pnpm guard`
- `pnpm typecheck`
- `git diff --check`
- `ruby -e 'require "yaml"; YAML.load_file(".github/workflows/nix-check.yml"); puts "nix-check.yml parses"'`
- `actionlint .github/workflows/nix-check.yml`
- `ruby -e 'require "yaml"; YAML.load_file(".github/workflows/release-beta.yml"); puts "release-beta.yml parses"'`
- `actionlint .github/workflows/release-beta.yml`
- `pnpm -C e2e test tests/packaged-smoke-workflow.test.ts`
- `ruby -e 'require "yaml"; YAML.load_file(".github/workflows/ci.yml"); YAML.load_file(".github/workflows/release-beta.yml"); puts "workflow yaml ok"'`
- `node --check .github/scripts/release/r2/publish-platform.ts && node --check .github/scripts/release/r2/publish-beta-metadata.ts && node --check .github/scripts/release/r2/verify-beta-metadata.ts && node --check .github/scripts/release/r2/summary-beta.ts`
- Local fake-AWS publish smoke for `publish-platform.ts` + `publish-beta-metadata.ts`
- Local R2 review behavior checks: partial beta does not write `beta/latest/metadata.json`, complete beta does, empty platform reports fail, and the verifier checks report files.
- Playwright partition list checks:
  - `--grep-invert 'home starters|home hero'`: 15 tests

Remote validation:

- CI `26085031858`: success, 172s elapsed.
  - Previous final CI sample `26082246926`: 175s.
  - Initial traced CI baseline `26080283519`: 229s.
  - Playwright split jobs: `core` 146s, `starters` 127s.

## Summary
Second drop of the WordPress plugin. Posts now carry **every** field MDDB could plausibly want to index.

### Mapper — full meta capture ([includes/class-mapper.php](integrations/wordpress-plugin/includes/class-mapper.php))
- Every \`get_post_meta($id, '', false)\` row. Scalars cast to string, serialized arrays/objects JSON-encoded.

- ACF — if \`get_fields()\` is available, parsed values land under \`acf:<name>\` keys (URLs, post IDs, repeater arrays — not raw \`wp_postmeta\` blobs).
- New \`mddb_sync_meta\` filter: \`apply_filters('mddb_sync_meta', \$meta, \$post)\` — redact secrets, drop \`_edit_lock\`/\`_edit_last\`, inject your own fields.

### SEO normaliser ([includes/class-seo.php](integrations/wordpress-plugin/includes/class-seo.php))
Detects **Yoast**, **RankMath**, **SEOPress** and emits stable keys: \`seoSource\`, \`seoTitle\`, \`seoDescription\`, \`seoFocusKeyword\`, \`seoCanonical\`, \`seoRobots*\`, \`ogTitle\`/\`ogDescription\`/\`ogImage\`, \`twitterTitle\`/\`twitterDescription\`/\`twitterImage\`. Raw plugin meta keys still ship from the post-meta dump. Source with most filled fields wins (Yoast tie-breaker).

Without this PR, that run produces the old weekly digest format. With it, every Pro vendor gets the new 12-section AI Visibility Intelligence Report.

## Changes to `jobs/scheduledReports.js`

The Monday `'0 8 * * 1'` cron block is replaced. New flow per vendor:

3. **Write AgentRun** — `agentName: 'reporter'` with reportNumber + score

author: takecy
body:
## 概要

issue #28 の **基盤 PR**。macOS native メニューバー (File / Edit submenu) を追加し、`Cmd+O` でネイティブダイアログから画像を開く 4 番目の入力経路を導入する。menu / toolbar / JS keydown の三重登録 + source-aware de-dupe を共有層で実装。

対応する identifier (issue #28 本文):

- `[A-2]` File メニュー (`Open...` / `Save As...` / `Copy to Clipboard`)
- `[A-3]` Edit メニュー (`Undo` / `Redo` / `Delete`)
- `[B-1]` `MenuEvent` を Rust 側で受けて `app.emit("menu-action", id)`
- `[B-2]` フロント側で `listen()` 購読 + 既存ハンドラ呼び出し
- `[C-1]` ネイティブファイルダイアログから画像取得
- `[C-2]` 取得パスを既存の `useImageLoader.ts` `file-open-requested` 系統に流入
- `[C-4]` Rust 側 `safe_image_canonical` で trust boundary 適用
- `[C-5]` README/CLAUDE.md/site docs の「画像入力経路を 3 → 4」更新

**`[C-3]`** (capability に `dialog:allow-open` 追加) は **構造的に不要**: 新設計では Rust 内部で `tauri_plugin_dialog::DialogExt` を直接呼ぶため、Frontend からの `dialog:allow-open` invoke 経路を使わない。

Refs #28

## 設計判断

### 1. Frontend `@tauri-apps/plugin-dialog#open()` を意図的に使わない

JS の `open()` は path 解決後に **内部で `scope.allow_file(&path)` を自動実行** する (`tauri-plugin-dialog-2.7.1/src/commands.rs:203`)。これは Rust 側検証より前に renderer の fs scope が広がってしまうため、`[C-4]` の「trust boundary 一本化」要件に反する。新規 Rust command `pick_and_open_image` 内で `DialogExt::dialog().file().pick_file(...)` を直接呼ぶ設計に統一し、検証通過時のみ手動で `scope.allow_file(&canonical)` する。

### 2. `safe_image_canonical` (旧 `is_safe_image_path`) の honest scope

`is_safe_image_path: bool` を `safe_image_canonical: Option<PathBuf>` に変更し、検証通過時の canonical path を返す。これにより `pick_first_open_image_path` / `RunEvent::Opened` / 新 `pick_and_open_image` callback がすべて canonical path を `handle_opened_image_path` に渡し、`scope.allow_file` と emit が **同一の path 文字列** で動作 (= path 文字列不一致排除)。

**ただし TOCTOU 完全解消ではない**: `symlink_metadata` → 拡張子チェック → `canonicalize` → `allow_file` → 実 `readFile` は path 文字列ベースで分離しており、親ディレクトリ制御攻撃モデルでは residual race が残る。完全防御 (`O_NOFOLLOW` FD 保持 / bytes 化) は別 issue。

### 3. Source-aware copy de-dupe (App.tsx 共有層)

`Cmd+Z` / `Cmd+Shift+Z` / `Cmd+Shift+C` は menu / keydown (CanvasArea) / toolbar (ActionBar Copy) の最大 3 経路から発火する。`App.tsx` に共有 `lastFiredRef` + `shouldSuppress(id, { record })` を置き、100ms 同一 id 連続発火を抑制。

**Copy のみ source-aware**:
- menu (`record=false`): best-effort、WKWebView の transient user activation を失う可能性 → flag を立てない
- keydown / toolbar (`record=true`): 信頼経路 → flag を立てる

これで menu が先発火して失敗しても、後続の keydown / toolbar が rescue できる。逆に keydown / toolbar が先発火して成功したら menu は suppress される。

Undo / Redo は menu / keydown どちらも信頼経路なので record=true で対称。

### 4. テキスト編集中の Cmd+Z bail-out

`useMenuAction` の handler 内で `document.activeElement` を判定 (`HTMLTextAreaElement` / `HTMLInputElement` / `isContentEditable`)。text-edit context 時は `document.execCommand("undo")` / `"redo"` に分岐し、canvas undo を発火させない。`CanvasArea.tsx` keydown の既存 bail-out と同じ判定ロジック。

### 5. Edit → Delete: Backspace accelerator は付けない + menu-click 経路も text-edit bail-out

macOS は menu accelerator として登録されたキーを **keydown より優先** して menu handler に流すため、`MenuItemBuilder::accelerator("Backspace")` を付けると **text input にフォーカスがあるときの Backspace が canvas shape 削除に化ける**。codex-rescue で HIGH として指摘され、本 PR (commit `fe50c1c`) で対応:

- **lib.rs**: `edit_delete` MenuItemBuilder から `.accelerator("Backspace")` を削除。menubar 表示のみで accelerator は無し。Backspace キー入力は JS keydown 経路 (`CanvasArea.tsx:558-561` の text-edit bail-out 付き) に直接届く
- **useMenuAction.ts**: menu **click** 経由でも `isInTextEditContext()` を判定し、text input focus 中なら shape 削除を skip (defense-in-depth)
- `execCommand("delete")` は **使わない** (forward-delete = Cmd+Delete で Backspace と意味が異なるため、呼ぶと UX 混乱)

PR レビュー時に macOS 上で以下を確認:

- **Phase 3** (2.0s): 정면 얼굴 + 초록 스캔 라인 sweep (`scan-move` 애니메이션 활성화)
- **Phase 4** (0.9s): 왼쪽 프로필 얼굴 (`figma_face3.png`) 표시 후 루프 재시작

- `DOMContentLoaded` → `startIntroAnim()` 호출 (초기 진입 시 루프 시작)
- `startTest()` → `stopIntroAnim()` 호출 (테스트 시작 시 루프 중단)

- `async/await` + `while(introRunning)` 루프 패턴으로 정확한 페이즈 타이밍 제어

## Summary

- Removes the hardcoded `CORE_MODULES` bulk insert from `001_initial_schema`; module rows are seeded in a dedicated migration instead.
- Adds Alembic revisions `026`–`029` to seed the platform permission vocabulary (`read`, `create`, `edit`, `delete`) and a hierarchical module catalog (L1–L4) under User Management, Configurator, Master Data, and Visitpad (including Rx column sections).
- Links every active module at **level ≥ 2** to all four permissions via `module_permissions` (`{module_slug}:{permission_slug}`). L1 modules intentionally have no junction rows.

## Migrations

| Revision | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `026_master_data_catalog_permissions` | Seed `global_master.permissions` (read, create, edit, delete) |
| `027_core_modules_catalog` | Seed module tree (UM, configurator, master-data, visitpad L3/L4) |
| `028_core_module_permissions_catalog` | Link L2+ modules to all four permissions |
| `029_add_delete_permission_catalog` | Idempotent add of `delete` for DBs that ran `028` before delete existed |

## Local reset (master-data only)

```bash
PGPASSWORD=hims psql -h localhost -p 5433 -U hims -d hims_dev -c "
DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS global_master CASCADE;
DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS tenant_master CASCADE;
DELETE FROM public.alembic_version;
"
cd modules/master-data && uv run alembic upgrade head
```

Or full stack: `make db-reset` (includes `master-data:migrate` via `make db-migrate`).

## Test plan

- [ ] Fresh DB: drop `global_master` / `tenant_master`, clear `alembic_version`, run `alembic upgrade head` — expect head `029`
- [ ] Verify four permissions: `read`, `create`, `edit` (action `update`), `delete`
- [ ] Verify module counts by level (L1 core + visitpad-templates, L2 catalog sections, L3 visitpad catalogs, L4 rx-column sections)
- [ ] Verify each L2+ module has four `module_permissions` rows
- [ ] Smoke: `GET /api/v1/master-data/modules` and `GET /api/v1/master-data/permissions` on a running master-data service
